messages.author: 5f950c9713997d19
messages.subject: Changing Parameters amongst models on-the-fly
parts:
Hi TMB users

I have two models, the difference between which is the list of parameters used (there are other differences but not germane to my question). I am exploring if I can change the PARAMETER declarations in the cpp file dependent on an input model flag. For example,

...

DATA_INTEGER(model_no);   where model_no is input as an integer such as 1, 2, etc
...

I tried using the switch command (with the appropriate parms set up in the r file) as:

  switch(model_no)
  {
   case 1:
    PARAMETER_MATRIX(parm1_mat);
    PARAMETER_VECTOR(parm1_vect);
   break;

   case 2:
    PARAMETER_VECTOR(parm2_vect);
    PARAMETER(parm2);
   break;
  }
 
but this doesn't seem to work. Can switch or other c++ syntax be used to change TMB parameters on-the-fly? Am I missing something?

Any insight is much appreciated.

Bob

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Changing Parameters amongst models on-the-fly
parts:
Hi Bob, you can use the "map" feature to selectively turn off parameter estimation while calling MakeADFun, then use a flag inside the template for your calculations. People often use this for similar reasons as what I understand you're asking for. I'm not aware of any examples with the map feature but I think it's documented on the R side. 

It actually would be a good example to add to the list: full demonstration of the map capabilities.

-Cole

messages.author: 90b303eef43fd993
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Changing Parameters amongst models on-the-fly
parts:
In addition to the map feature here are a few more options:

1. Control the case you're in from R by passing zero-length objects:

PARAMETER_MATRIX(parm1_mat);
PARAMETER_VECTOR(parm1_vect);
PARAMETER_VECTOR(parm2_vect);
PARAMETER(parm2);

int model_no;
if (parm1_mat.size() > 0) model_no = 1;
if (parm2_vect.size() > 0) model_no = 2;


2. Conditionally pass parameter objects (but not until you need them):

DATA_INTEGER(model_no);

if (model_no == 1) {
  PARAMETER_MATRIX(parm1_mat);   // Local to the branch
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(parm1_vect);  // Local to the branch
  // Here comes procedure depending on parameters
}

Hi Kasper

I tried the if syntax to select between models and found out a few things. 

If a PARAMETER declaration is within an if loop, then pretty much all references to the declared parameter have to be within that loop. I tried using a parameter outside the loop and I got 'not declared in scope' errors. This was also the case for a REPORT statement. 

I also tried the switch command rather than the if syntax and couldn't get it to work. Not sure why as I have other code (e.g. SAM) in which it does. I'll use the if syntax unless you or anyone else can identify some special issues with the switch command that I should be aware of.

Thanks again

messages.author: 90b303eef43fd993
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Changing Parameters amongst models on-the-fly
parts:
Hi Bob,

This is all as expected: Calculations referring to a parameter declared inside a block must be within that same block. The same holds for REPORT statements.

However, note the following trick to get a parameter from 'local scope' to 'global scope':

Type a_;
if (true) {
  PARAMETER(a);
  a_ = a;
}

The switch statement cannot be used as variable declarations inside 'switch' are not allowed.

Cheers,
Kasper

People often use this for similar reasons as what I understand you're asking for. I'm not aware of any examples with the map feature but I think it's documented on the R side. 

It actually would be a good example to add to the list: full demonstration of the map capabilities.

-Cole

Hi TMB users

I have two models, the difference between which is the list of parameters used (there are other differences but not germane to my question). I am exploring if I can change the PARAMETER declarations in the cpp file dependent on an input model flag. For example,

...

DATA_INTEGER(model_no);   where model_no is input as an integer such as 1, 2, etc
...

I tried using the switch command (with the appropriate parms set up in the r file) as:

  switch(model_no)
  {
   case 1:
    PARAMETER_MATRIX(parm1_mat);
    PARAMETER_VECTOR(parm1_vect);
   break;

   case 2:
    PARAMETER_VECTOR(parm2_vect);

  }
 
but this doesn't seem to work. Can switch or other c++ syntax be used to change TMB parameters on-the-fly? Am I missing something?

Any insight is much appreciated.
